messages:
acme_engineer: Hi team — after upgrading to github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.9.2 our build breaks during CI, blocking a deploy. Can someone help?

sam_support: Sorry you hit this — can you paste your go.mod and the exact error?

acme_engineer: Repro steps:
```
go version go1.20.5
module acme-pay
require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.9.2
# no replace in our project

go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v0.9.2
```
Error: 
```
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v0.9.2: no matching versions for query "v0.9.2"
# or sometimes
module declares its path: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go
```

sam_support: Thanks — both errors are informative. @leo_eng can you investigate whether the tag is published and what the tagged go.mod contains?

leo_eng: Running remote checks now:
```
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk.git
git show refs/tags/v0.9.2:go.mod
```
The tag exists, but the tagged go.mod shows `module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go` (different path). That mismatch will make the proxy and `go get` complain when querying the original module path.

anya_release: Ugh — CI created that tag from release/0.9. There was a merged change that renamed the module path in a feature branch and it made it into the release branch before tagging. CI: "created tag v0.9.2 from commit abcd1234" (release log ref).

leo_eng: That explains it. GOPROXY (proxy.golang.org) will not serve a version whose go.mod claims a different module path than the requested module. So consumers of github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk see the errors you pasted.

sam_support: Customer is blocked — what short-term options can we give them?

leo_eng: Short-term workarounds: 1) pin to v0.9.1 until we cut a fixed release, 2) use a commit pseudo-version that points to a commit before the rename, e.g. `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v0.0.0-20250101-abcdef123456`, or 3) add a local `replace` in their go.mod pointing to a checked-out local repo or a corrected module path. Example replace: `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../go-sdk-local` or to a pseudo-version as above. Also, `GOPROXY=direct go get ...` can help if the upstream git tag is changed and the proxy has cache issues.

acme_engineer: We tried GOPROXY=direct and still hit the module path mismatch error.

leo_eng: Right — direct still checks go.mod inside the tag and will reject mismatched module paths. The only way around that without a new tag is to use a replace / pseudo-version or stay on v0.9.1.

anya_release: We should not force-replace or re-tag v0.9.2. Plan: cut v0.9.3 that restores the correct module path in go.mod and publish it. Also add a short release note calling out that v0.9.2 had an accidental module-path rename and is broken. We'll add a CI guard to prevent go.mod path drift into release tags.

leo_eng: My proposed steps to create the fix tag:
```
git checkout -b fix/restore-modpath abcd1234
# edit go.mod -> module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk
git commit -am "restore module path for v0.9.3"
git tag v0.9.3
git push origin fix/restore-modpath && git push origin v0.9.3
```
Then wait for GitHub and module proxies to pick up v0.9.3. If the customer still fails, ask them to `go clean -modcache` and retry.

ci-bot: release-pipeline: tagging v0.9.3 in 10m. Will post back after push. Note: we will not reuse v0.9.2.

sam_support: ETA for v0.9.3? Need to update the customer's ticket and they are in a deploy window.

anya_release: Cutting the tag now. I'll run the pipeline and confirm when GitHub tag and release assets are pushed. I will also add a short advisory on the release page.

ci-bot: release-pipeline: pushed tag v0.9.3 and created GitHub tag. Proxies may take a few minutes to index. If the customer still sees errors, have them run: `go clean -modcache` and then `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v0.9.3`. If they still fail, ask them to try `GOPROXY=direct` and attach the exact `go env` output.

sam_support: I'll relay the workarounds and the expected v0.9.3 availability to Acme. Will follow up once they confirm the build succeeds. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
